  <section v="0">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section provides the header and date for the maamar.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">B"S.</t>
    <t s="1">Shabbos Parshas Haazinu,</t>
    <t s="2">12 Tishrei 5742</t>
  </section>
  <section v="1">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section notes that the maamar is a discourse delivered orally.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">(A discourse)</t>
  </section>
  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains the verse about the eagle, distinguishing between simple eagle-like mercy and a higher level of mercy, and states that the highest matters are found specifically in the lowest realm.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">“As an eagle stirs up its nest, hovers over its young, etc.”¹</t>
    <t s="1">Now, what is written before it?²</t>
    <t s="2">“He found him in a desert land,”</t>
    <t s="3">And afterwards it concludes:³</t>
    <t s="4">“Hashem alone will lead him.”</t>
    <t s="5">Now, the simple explanation of this is,</t>
    <t s="6">that the Holy One, blessed be He, conducts Himself with the Jewish people with mercy, like the eagle that hovers over its young</t>
    <t s="7">(as Rashi explains).</t>
    <t s="8">That is to say,</t>
    <t s="9">that there is the mercy of an eagle in its simple sense,</t>
    <t s="10">and there is a mercy that is like an eagle and above it.</t>
    <t s="11">Now, all the matters in the Torah exist in all the worlds, up to the highest level,</t>
    <t s="12">and from this it is understood,</t>
    <t s="13">that just as there are these two levels in this physical world</t>
    <t s="14">(an eagle and like an eagle),</t>
    <t s="15">so too is it in the worlds above it,</t>
    <t s="16">the worlds of Beriah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah,</t>
    <t s="17">up to the world of Atzilus,</t>
    <t s="18">for even though it has ten Sefiros, it is a world of unity,</t>
    <t s="19">nevertheless, within it there is also the aspect of “eagle,” which is the attribute of mercy of Atzilus,</t>
    <t s="20">and within it there is the aspect of “like an eagle,”</t>
    <t s="21">meaning a mercy that is above the attribute of mercy.⁴</t>
    <t s="22">However, even so, the essence of the Torah is below, as the statement:⁵</t>
    <t s="23">“The Torah is not in heaven,”</t>
    <t s="24">and as the teaching of the Maggid of Mezeritch⁶</t>
    <t s="25">on the Sages’ statement:⁷</t>
    <t s="26">“Know what is above you,”</t>
    <t s="27">that all the matters above are dependent upon you,</t>
    <t s="28">upon the service of man who is below,</t>
    <t s="29">and particularly after the Giving of the Torah, when the Torah was given below and is not in heaven</t>
    <t s="30">(as above).</t>
    <t s="31">And furthermore,</t>
    <t s="32">that everything higher descends lower,⁸</t>
    <t s="33">meaning that the most elevated matter</t>
    <t s="34">(in the Torah)</t>
    <t s="35">is found specifically below,</t>
    <t s="36">and from this it is also understood regarding the matter of the eagle,</t>
    <t s="37">that this verse includes both extremes,</t>
    <t s="38">that the most supernal mercy is drawn down specifically below, in the place where there is the simple mercy of an eagle.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
